_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Both engines derive workload shape AND pass/fail thresholds from this file. Nothing below is duplicated inside workload.jmx or workload.js: k6 reads this file directly with open() at init, and JMeter -- which cannot read JSON -- gets it via tools/gen_jmeter_props.py, which projects it into the .properties file every ${__P(...)} in the plan resolves against. Change a number here and both engines change together. Change it in only one of them and the cross-engine divergence check catches you.

cross_engine._readme: If JMeter and k6 measure the same service under the same workload, their numbers must land in the same neighbourhood. A wide gap does not mean the service is slow -- it means the two scripts are not the same test, and the verdict is untrustworthy no matter which way it fell.

teeth._readme: Fault injected via Toxiproxy for `make prove-teeth`. Both engines MUST report FAIL under this. An engine that still passes is not passing -- it is blind.
